article_content: On 13 February 1945, British rifleman Victor Gregg, aged 25, was being held by Germans in a makeshift prison in Dresden along with hundreds of other men who had been sentenced to death. Gregg had been sentenced to death for burning down the soap factory where he was sent to work as punishment for twice attempting to escape his POW camp. Despite a widespread understanding that the Allies would preserve Dresden's cultural heritage, just as the Germans had refrained from attacking Oxford, the city was bombed. The bombing was catastrophic, turning men into 'human torches' and causing widespread destruction. Gregg eventually escaped and made his way to the advancing Russian lines before being flown back to Britain.

Gregg havia estat condemnat a mort per incendiar la fàbrica de sabó on havia estat enviat a treballar com a càstig per haver intentat escapar dues vegades del seu camp de presoners de guerra. Tot i l'enteniment generalitzat que els Aliats preservarien el patrimoni cultural de Dresden, de la mateixa manera que els alemanys havien evitat atacar Oxford, la ciutat va ser bombardejada. El bombardeig va ser devastador, convertint els homes en 'torxes humanes' i causant una destrucció àmplia. Gregg finalment va aconseguir escapar i es va dirigir cap a les línies russes abans de ser traslladat a Britània.

article_content: By Tara Brady. PUBLISHED: 00:38 EST, 6 March 2014. UPDATED: 07:00 EST, 6 March 2014. The European Union has named 18 Ukrainians whose assets will be frozen, including ousted President Viktor Yanukovych, his son, and former Prime Minister Mykola Azarov. The EU revealed the names of those believed to be responsible for embezzling state funds in Ukraine. The list includes Yanukovych's closest aides. The EU said it was freezing assets of Ukrainian officials held in the EU. China has agreed with the US that Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity must be respected. Former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov and his son will also have their assets frozen. US National Security Adviser Susan Rice spoke to Chinese State Councilor Yang Jiechi about the Ukraine situation. The US has engaged in diplomatic efforts to oppose Russia's deployment of troops in Crimea. A video emerged of UN special envoy Robert Serry being forced to take refuge after being threatened at gunpoint. Serry was escorted out in a vehicle surrounded by demonstrators waving Russian flags.

article_content: (CNN) -- New York City's bright neon lights are iconic, but they're disappearing. Architectural conservator Thomas Rinaldi started documenting the city's historic neon signs six years ago. 'Old neon signs had caught my attention for many years, but they began to disappear at such a rate that I felt a real sense of urgency to photograph them before they vanished,' Rinaldi said. The result is the book 'New York Neon,' a visual tour of the remaining exposed-tube neon signs in the five boroughs. Most of the 200 signs featured are from the early- and mid-20th century.

'Els senyals de neó antics havien cridat la meva atenció durant anys, però van començar a desaparèixer a un ritme alarmant, així que vaig sentir la necessitat de fotografiar-los abans que desapareguessin,' va dir Rinaldi. El resultat és el llibre 'New York Neon,' una visita visual pels senyals de neó que encara romanen als cinc districtes.

article_content: The stunning scenery of Dinorwic Quarry in Snowdonia, North Wales, bears a striking resemblance to the fictional realm of 'The Lord of the Rings'. JRR Tolkien, the celebrated author of the epic fantasy series, is known to have drawn inspiration from the Welsh language when creating the Elvish dialect. Spanning over 700 acres, Dinorwic Quarry was once the second-largest slate quarry in the world before its closure in 1969. Photographer Matthew Growcoot's captivating images of the quarry evoke a sense of adventure, reminiscent of traversing Middle Earth. Tolkien's affinity for Wales is well-documented, with the Elvish language mirroring the sounds and structure of the Welsh language.

article_content: BANGKOK: Car production in Thailand dropped 8.45% in September from the previous year to 164,093 units, as domestic sales slumped, the Federation of Thai Industries said on Tuesday. Thailand's domestic car sales in September contracted 16.27% year-on-year, following a revised 11.7% decline in August, as banks tighten auto lending, said Surapong Paisitpattanapong, spokesperson for the Federation of Thai Industries' automotive industry division. The country's September car production decline was less severe compared to a 12.27% contraction in August. Thailand is a regional vehicle production and export base for some of the world's top carmakers, including Toyota and Honda.

Les vendes nacionals de cotxes al setembre van contreure un '16,27%' any rere any, després d'un declivi revisat de l''11,7%' a l'agost, ja que els bancs van estrènyer els préstecs per a automòbils, va dir Surapong Paisitpattanapong, portaveu de la divisió de la indústria automotriu de la Federació d'Indústries de Tailàndia. article_content: (CNN) -- Police in New Jersey arrested a 16-year-old teenager in connection with a public-address-system announcement telling 'all blacks' to leave a Wal-Mart store, a police spokesman said. The boy is from Atlantic County, New Jersey, said Deputy Police Chief John Dalesandro of the Washington Township Police Department. The suspect was arrested on Friday in Atlantic County on bias intimidation and harassment charges, police said in a statement on Saturday. He is in the custody of his parents, police said. Gloucester County prosecutors say that shortly before 5 p.m. on March 14, an unidentified male accessed the public address system at the Turnersville, New Jersey, Wal-Mart Supercenter Store. 'All blacks need to leave the store,' the voice announced. Store management contacted the Washington Township Police Department, which opened an investigation in conjunction with the county prosecutor's office, Dalesandro said. Wal-Mart corporate spokesman Lorenzo Lopez said the company is 'just as appalled by this as anyone.' He emphasized that Wal-Mart is working with law enforcement officials. 'Whoever did this is wrong and acted in an inappropriate manner,' Lopez said. 'Clearly this is unacceptable.' Law enforcement officials said that Wal-Mart is now acting to limit the public address feature to a smaller number of in-store telephones. Lopez confirmed that the New Jersey store is updating its intercom systems and that the company is reviewing the incident to see if there are any lessons for the retailer's other 4,000-plus American stores.

El noi és d'Atlantic County, Nova Jersey, segons el cap adjunt de policia John Dalesandro del Departament de Policia de Washington Township. El sospitós va ser detingut divendres a Atlantic County per càrrecs d'intimidació i assetjament, segons un comunicat de la policia. Està sota la custòdia dels seus pares. Els fiscals del comtat de Gloucester expliquen que poc abans de les 5 de la tarda del 14 de març, un home sense identificar va accedir al sistema d'adreça pública de Wal-Mart a Turnersville, Nova Jersey. 'Tots els negres han de deixar la botiga', va dir la veu. La direcció de la botiga va contactar amb el Departament de Policia de Washington Township, que va iniciar una investigació amb l'oficina del fiscal del comtat, segons Dalesandro. El portaveu de Wal-Mart, Lorenzo Lopez, va dir que l'empresa 'està tan indignada com qualsevol altre'. Va destacar que Wal-Mart col·labora amb els funcionaris de seguretat. 'Qui va fer això està equivocat i va actuar de manera inapropiada', va dir Lopez. 'Això és clarament inacceptable'. Els funcionaris de seguretat van dir que Wal-Mart limitarà la funció d'adreça pública a menys telèfons de la botiga. Lopez va confirmar que la botiga de Nova Jersey està actualitzant els sistemes d'intercomunicació i que l'empresa revisarà l'incident per extreure lliçons per a les seves més de 4.000 botigues als Estats Units.

article_content: Doctors say 24-year-old Ashley Caughey has only months to live after malignant bone cancer spread throughout her body. She worries she won't see her daughter Paisley's first birthday. Ashley refused chemotherapy during pregnancy to give birth to Paisley last year. She had just gotten engaged to her now-husband Jonathan when diagnosed with osteosarcoma in her leg. 'The doctor I visited repeatedly probably cost me my life,' Ashley says. She underwent surgery to remove her knee and femur, and doctors advised chemotherapy. Ashley gave birth to Paisley in June; shortly after, she learned the cancer had spread to her body and brain. The couple married in November, with Ashley's 6-year-old son Braiden walking her down the aisle. Ashley started radiation treatment after Paisley's birth, but doctors say she now has only a few months to live. Ashley is documenting her journey on camera so her kids can see her fighting.

S'acabava de comprometre amb el seu marit Jonathan quan va rebre el diagnòstic d'osteosarcoma a la cama. 'El metge al qual vaig anar repetidament probablement em va costar la vida,' diu Ashley. Va ser operada per eliminar el genoll i el fèmur, i els metges li van aconsellar quimioteràpia. Ashley va donar a llum a Paisley al juny; poc després, va saber que el càncer s'havia estès pel seu cos i cervell. La parella es va casar al novembre, amb el seu fill de 6 anys, Braiden, acompanyant-la a l'altar. article_content: KOLKATA: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee to appear before it on November 9 in connection with the alleged school jobs scam, a TMC leader said on Wednesday. Banerjee will appear before the ED on Thursday, West Bengal Women and Child Welfare Minister and TMC spokesperson Shashi Panja said, alleging that the party's national general secretary is a victim of 'vendetta politics'. The BJP was accused by her of indulging in such politics to 'harass' leaders ahead of crucial elections early next year. State BJP spokesperson Shamik Bhattacharya responded that the party doesn't believe in 'vendetta politics' and that the ED's actions are under court supervision. The ED had earlier summoned Banerjee on October 9, after he missed the October 3 summons to participate in a TMC protest rally in New Delhi, demanding the immediate release of central funds to the state. Banerjee was questioned by the ED for nearly nine hours on September 13 in the teacher recruitment scam and had claimed the interrogation was politically motivated. The two-time TMC MP had also been questioned twice by the ED in the coal pilferage case, in 2021 and 2022.

Banerjee compareixerà davant l'ED dijous, va dir la ministra de Benestar de la Dona i el Nen de Bengala Occidental i portaveu del TMC Shashi Panja, al·legant que el secretari general nacional del partit és víctima de 'política de venjança'. El BJP va ser acusat per ella de participar en aquesta política per 'assetjar' líders abans de les eleccions crucials de principis de l'any vinent. El portaveu del BJP estatal, Shamik Bhattacharya, va respondre que el partit no creu en la 'política de venjança' i que les accions de l'ED estan sota la supervisió del tribunal. L'ED ja havia citat Banerjee el 9 d'octubre, després que ell es perdés la citació del 3 d'octubre per participar en una manifestació de protesta del TMC a Nova Delhi, demanant l'alliberament immediat de fons centrals a l'estat. Banerjee va ser interrogat per l'ED durant gairebé nou hores el 13 de setembre en el cas de frau en la contractació de professors i havia afirmat que l'interrogatori estava motivat políticament. El diputat del TMC dues vegades també havia estat interrogat dues vegades per l'ED en el cas de malversació de carbó, el 2021 i el 2022.

article_content: At a Chinese zoo, a shocking incident occurred when a newborn elephant calf was attacked by its mother shortly after birth. The mother elephant, upon giving birth to the calf named Zhuangzhuang on August 30, immediately stepped on him. Veterinarians initially believed the incident was accidental and, after treating the calf's injuries, returned him to his mother two hours later. However, the mother elephant's aggressive behavior continued as she attempted to stamp on the calf again. The keepers intervened, rescuing Zhuangzhuang and taking him into their care. The calf, visibly distressed, cried for five hours after being separated from his mother. Despite the initial trauma, Zhuangzhuang is now thriving under the care of his keepers at the Shendiaoshan Wild Animal Natural Reserve Area in Rongcheng, Shandong province. The reasons behind the mother elephant's violent behavior towards her calf remain unclear.

article_content: Chris Chamberlain, a 49-year-old IT worker from Bromley, London, has spent over two years creating 'Jewel of the Universe', a detailed mosaic map of the world. This artwork is made up of 333,000 hand-cut glass pieces and features 1,238 jewels, including topaz, amethysts, and sapphires, to highlight significant cities and rivers. Using NASA photographs for reference, Chamberlain ensured the mosaic's geographical accuracy and trained himself to be ambidextrous to prevent repetitive strain injury. Chamberlain has listed 'Jewel of the Universe' on eBay for £250,000, with the proceeds going towards projects in Sierra Leone, where his wife Theodora was born.

article_content: The battle for control of Ramadi, Anbar's capital, is shifting in favor of Iraqi and tribal forces fighting ISIS, Iraqi officials said on Monday. Iraqi forces, aided by coalition airstrikes, have pushed back ISIS militants and retaken lost territory after ISIS's coordinated Friday assault. They've regained control of Ramadi's sole military supply line from a nearby airbase, according to Faleh al-Issawi, Anbar's deputy governor. While fighting persists in parts of Ramadi and an eastern suburb, al-Issawi is optimistic about retaking the city if coalition airstrikes continue. The battle has been raging since Friday, 1,000 feet from Anbar's government complex. ISIS has retreated further, and fighting is less intense, officials say. At least 41 people, including security forces, tribesmen, and civilians, have been killed since Friday. Casualties include 23 executed members of the al-Bu Fahd tribe in areas retaken from ISIS.

La lluita continua en parts de Ramadi, però al-Issawi és optimista que les forces iraquianes recuperin la ciutat amb atacs aeris de la coalició. La batalla ha estat intensa des de divendres, prop del complex governamental d'Anbar. L'ISIS s'ha retirat i la lluita és menys intensa. Almenys 41 morts des de divendres, inclosos 23 membres de la tribu al-Bu Fahd executats.

article_content: Some airline passengers stuck waiting on the tarmac at the Seattle airport were treated to a soothing serenade courtesy of members of the Seattle Symphony. Alaska Airlines flight 550 passengers, en route to Palm Springs, California, on Sunday, had made it as far as the runway when their plane was turned around and sent back to the gate due to technical issues. While the irritable travelers waited, they were treated to some comforting music from a string quartet that happened to be on board with their instruments. 'We were lucky to be sitting amongst a string quartet who broke out their instruments and played for us,' said passenger Addie Bogart. The Seattle Symphony violinists, Mikhail Shmidt and Elisa Barston, violist Susan Gulkis Assadi, and cellist Walter Gray, were behind the impromptu concert. The quartet was en route to Palm Springs, where they were to play two benefit concerts. 'Made everyone's night!' Bogart said. 'It almost made us forget we were two hours late to Palm Springs.' Unbeknownst to many on the plane, they were treated to a free concert from newly minted Grammy winners. The Seattle Symphony won its first Grammy award on Sunday for Best Contemporary Classical Composition for its recording of a commissioned piece by composer John Luther Adams.

article_content: By Timothy Obiezu October 24, 2023 Nigerian authorities are hailing a 'landmark' London high court ruling that 'completely exonerated' Nigeria from $11 billion in damages stemming from a 'dubious' and 'corrupt' gas project between Africa's largest economy and a 'corrupt' private company. In a statement, Nigerian President Bola Tinubu lauded the London Business and Property Court's ruling in the 2010 gas deal, calling it a 'major victory' for the 'long exploited' African continent. 'Nation states will no longer be held hostage by economic conspiracies between private firms and solitary corrupt officials,' Tinubu said. Nigeria and Process and Industrial Developments, a firm based in the British Virgin Islands, signed the contract under 'unclear circumstances'. The deal fell through, and P&ID took the Nigerian government to court in Britain. In 2017, an arbitration tribunal ordered Nigeria to pay a $6.6 billion contract award and interest to P&ID. The government appealed that decision. The court said the company had paid a bribe to a Nigerian oil ministry official. The court also said that P&ID did not disclose that information when the deal failed to materialize and that two British lawyers stood to benefit if the court ruled in favor of the firm. Nigerian political analyst Rotimi Olawale said the decision is a 'huge relief' for Africa's biggest economy. 'Nigeria dodged a major bullet, knowing the foreign exchange issues the country is facing,' Olawale said. 'Getting a judgment of $11 billion would've been a big blow to Nigeria's financial situation.' The company's lawyers are 'disheartened' and considering next steps. The firm denied the fraud allegations and accused Nigeria of 'incompetence and corruption'. Nigeria's economy has been struggling with inflation and debts. Government reform policies have seen Nigeria's foreign exchange reserve dwindle, increasing the scramble for U.S. dollars. The $11 billion would have been about one-third of Nigeria's foreign exchange reserves. Ebenezer Oyetakin, founder of the Anti-Corruption Network, said the ruling couldn't have come at a better time. 'It is an example of how many African countries have been mortgaging their economy,' he said. Olawale said Nigeria must address 'deep-seated' institutional corruption.
